# SL₂ is generated by its two root subgroups

`Langlands.GroupScheme.SpecialLinearBinaryRootGenerationStatement.{u}` is a
Prop-valued definition. This module defines the proposition and proves nothing.

## Statement

The proposition says: for every field `k : Type u`,

```text
IsGeneratedByFamily
  (fun _ : Fin 2 => VectorGroup.groupScheme (CommRingCat.of k) 1)
  ![SpecialLinear.BinaryRoot.upperMap (CommRingCat.of k),
    SpecialLinear.BinaryRoot.lowerMap (CommRingCat.of k)]
  (𝟙 (SpecialLinear.groupScheme (Fin 2) (CommRingCat.of k))).
```

In words: over every field `k`, the group scheme `SL₂` is generated by its
upper and lower root subgroups. Every closed subgroup of `SL₂` through which
both root homomorphisms `𝔾ₐ ⟶ SL₂` factor contains every point of `SL₂` on
every test scheme over `Spec k`.

Every ingredient is an existing declaration, used without change:

- `VectorGroup.groupScheme (CommRingCat.of k) 1` (from
  `Langlands.GroupScheme.VectorGroupQuotient`) is the additive group `𝔾ₐ`
  over `Spec k`. It is the spectrum of the polynomial ring in one variable.
- `SpecialLinear.groupScheme (Fin 2) (CommRingCat.of k)` (from
  `Langlands.GroupScheme.SpecialLinear`) is the affine group scheme `SL₂`
  over `Spec k`.
- `SpecialLinear.BinaryRoot.upperMap R` and `lowerMap R` (from
  `Langlands.GroupScheme.SpecialLinearBinaryRootGroups`) are the root
  homomorphisms `rootMap R` for the index pairs `(0, 1)` and `(1, 0)`. On
  every test scheme, `pointsEquiv_rootMap` shows that they send the
  coordinate `a` to the transvection
  `Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.transvection`. This is `[[1, a], [0, 1]]` for
  `upperMap` and `[[1, 0], [a, 1]]` for `lowerMap`. The published
  `isClosedSubgroup_rootMap` (from
  `Langlands.GroupScheme.SpecialLinearBinaryRootClosed`) proves that each
  map is a closed immersion. The published `mem_range_rootMap` identifies its
  image on every test scheme: it consists of the matrices whose entries agree
  with the identity matrix away from the root position. So the two images are
  exactly Milne's subgroups `U⁺` and `U⁻`, which are quoted below.
- `IsGeneratedByFamily A a i` (from `Langlands.GroupScheme.GeneratedFamily`)
  has three clauses. First, `i : H ⟶ G` is a closed subgroup
  (`IsClosedSubgroup`, meaning that the underlying morphism of schemes is a
  closed immersion). Second, every `a j` factors through `i`
  (`FactorsThrough`). Third, for every closed subgroup `q : K ⟶ G` through
  which every `a j` factors, `SubgroupFunctor.range i ≤ SubgroupFunctor.range q`.
  That is an inclusion of image subgroup functors on all test schemes over
  `Spec k`.

Here `i` is the identity of `SL₂`, so the first two clauses hold trivially.
The content of the proposition is the third clause: if a closed subgroup
`q : K ⟶ SL₂` lets both root homomorphisms factor through it, then every
point of `SL₂` on every test scheme lies in the image of `q`.

## Provenance (derived)

Source: J. S. Milne, *Algebraic Groups* (2017), registered as
`milne-2017-algebraic-groups` (SHA-256
`899b0f44f3c3ccfbaf5ed1cf9c180be7a8016b1c0e9709ca0c206304e5bd1cd0`). Printed page
numbers are given; the PDF page is the printed page plus 16.

- Section 20.g, printed p. 415 (PDF p. 431): "We use the following notation:
  T is the diagonal torus in SL2; […] U⁺ and U⁻ are the algebraic subgroups
  {[[1, ∗], [0, 1]]} and {[[1, 0], [∗, 1]]} of SL2." (The matrices are
  written row by row here.)
- Proposition 20.23, printed p. 415 (PDF p. 431):

  > PROPOSITION 20.23. The algebraic group SL2 is generated by its subgroups
  > U⁺ and U⁻.

  Milne's proof, printed p. 416 (PDF p. 432), reads in full: "Its Lie algebra
  is generated by the Lie algebras of U⁺ and U⁻ (10.2)."
- Generation, Proposition 2.51, printed p. 56 (PDF p. 72): "Let
  (φᵢ : Xᵢ → G)_{i∈I} be a family of regular maps from geometrically reduced
  algebraic schemes Xᵢ over k to an algebraic group G. There exists a smallest
  algebraic group H of G such that all φᵢ factor through H. Moreover, H is
  smooth." Section 2.h, printed p. 53 (PDF p. 69): "Such an algebraic subgroup
  is said to be generated by φ (or X) and is denoted by ⟨X, φ⟩." For
  subgroups, the proof of Corollary 10.17, printed p. 191 (PDF p. 207), says:
  "By definition, the algebraic subgroup generated by the Hᵢ is the smallest
  algebraic subgroup H of G such that all inclusion maps Hᵢ ↪ G factor
  through H".
- Algebraic subgroups, Definition 1.3, printed p. 7 (PDF p. 23): "An algebraic
  subgroup of an algebraic group (G, m_G) over k is an algebraic group
  (H, m_H) over k such that H is a k-subscheme of G and the inclusion map is a
  homomorphism of algebraic groups." Proposition 1.41, printed p. 18 (PDF
  p. 34): "Algebraic subgroups of algebraic groups are closed (in the Zariski
  topology)."

The official errata snapshot of 2026-11-02 (source ID
`milne-2017-algebraic-groups-errata-2026-11-02`, SHA-256
`a0c3a10dc376e1c9bd1de05b33beaf7d54e5f1ea7b408d594cfd70231a7ba0cf`) lists,
besides a note on where Notation 3.2 should be placed, Chapter 1 corrections
only on pp. 18 (the proof of 1.40), 20, 21 and 26, and
Chapter 2 corrections only on pp. 48, 51 and 60. Its Chapter 20 corrections are
only on pp. 417, 419 and 420 (the proof of 20.27, the statement and proof of
20.33, and a section reference). It has no Chapter 10 entries. None of these
concerns 20.23 or the results cited here.

The provenance is derived for four reasons:

1. Milne generates `SL₂` by the subgroups `U⁺` and `U⁻`, that is, by their
   inclusion maps. The formalization uses the root homomorphisms `𝔾ₐ ⟶ SL₂`
   instead. Each is a closed immersion with image `U⁺` or `U⁻`, by the published
   results named above. So a closed subgroup lets a root homomorphism factor
   through it exactly when it contains the corresponding subgroup.
2. Milne's algebraic subgroups of `SL₂` are closed subgroup schemes
   (Definition 1.3 and Proposition 1.41). They correspond to the competitors
   `q : K ⟶ SL₂` with `IsClosedSubgroup q`. Milne's "smallest" means
   containment of subschemes. For closed subschemes this is the same as
   containment of the subgroup functors `SubgroupFunctor.range` on all test
   schemes over `Spec k`.
3. The proposition states generation by asking the identity of `SL₂` to
   satisfy `IsGeneratedByFamily`. It does not name a separately constructed
   generated subgroup.
4. `k` lies in an arbitrary universe `u`. This is a formalization convention.

## For the proof (not part of this module)

The Library proves the proposition as `specialLinearBinaryRootGeneration` in
`SpecialLinearBinaryRootGenerationProof`.

Milne's one-line proof cites only Example 10.2. It applies Corollary 10.17,
printed p. 191 (PDF p. 207): "Let H₁, …, Hₙ be smooth algebraic subgroups of a
connected algebraic group G. If the Lie algebras of the Hᵢ generate Lie(G) as
a Lie algebra, then the Hᵢ generate G as an algebraic group." The hypotheses
hold for `G = SL₂`, `H₁ = U⁺` and `H₂ = U⁻`:

- `SL₂` is connected (2.42, printed p. 53: "The group SLn is connected"), and
  `U⁺ ≃ 𝔾ₐ` and `U⁻ ≃ 𝔾ₐ` are smooth.
- The tangent vectors of `SL₂` are the matrices `I + εA` over `k[ε]` with
  `det(I + εA) = 1 + ε·tr(A) = 1`. So `Lie(SL₂)` is the space `sl₂` of
  trace-zero matrices, with the commutator bracket inherited from `gl₂`
  (Theorem 10.23 and Remark 10.24, printed pp. 193–194). Similarly
  `Lie(U⁺) = k·X` and `Lie(U⁻) = k·Y`. By Example 10.2 (printed p. 187), the
  elements `X = [[0, 1], [0, 0]]`, `H = [[1, 0], [0, −1]]` and
  `Y = [[0, 0], [1, 0]]` form a basis of `sl₂`, and `[X, Y] = H`. So `X` and
  `Y` generate `sl₂` as a Lie algebra. This holds in every characteristic.
  In characteristic 2, `H` is the identity matrix, which has trace `2 = 0`.

The proof of 10.17 runs as follows; write `S` for the generated subgroup, to
avoid a clash with the matrix `H`. The subgroup `S` exists and is smooth
(2.51), and `Lie(U^±) ⊆ Lie(S) ⊆ Lie(SL₂)`. Since `Lie(S)` is a Lie
subalgebra, `Lie(S) = Lie(SL₂)`. Then Proposition 10.15 (printed p. 190: "Let
H ⊂ G be algebraic groups such that Lie(H) = Lie(G). If H is smooth and G is
connected, then H = G") gives `S = SL₂`. Every closed competitor contains `S`
by minimality, so it is all of `SL₂`.

In the Library, `FiniteGeneration.exists_smooth_generated_family` (in
`Langlands.GroupScheme.GeneratedFamily`) constructs a smooth connected affine
closed generated subgroup. `Lie.dimension_lt_of_proper_closedSubgroup` (in
`Langlands.GroupScheme.Lie.DimensionInduction`) shows that a proper smooth
closed subgroup of a smooth connected affine group has strictly smaller Lie
dimension.

An alternative route, not Milne's, avoids Lie brackets. It uses the published
rational-point generation `SpecialLinear.BinaryRoot.root_ranges_sup_eq_top`
over an algebraic closure `k̄`. Base change of a competitor `K` to `k̄`
contains `U^±_{k̄}`, so `K(k̄) = SL₂(k̄)`. A closed subscheme of the reduced
finite-type `k̄`-scheme `SL₂,k̄` that contains every `k̄`-point is everything.
Hence `K_{k̄} → SL₂,k̄` is an isomorphism, and so is `K → SL₂`, by faithfully
flat descent.
